mainTopic: Being treated by non-Jews for a מכה של חלל: what counts as internal, gums and teeth and צפדינא, why רבי יוחנן's treatment was allowed, and a list of dangerous ailments and their remedies
overview: The גמרא finishes the second version of רבי יוחנן's rule: one may not be treated by an idolater for a מכה של חלל. It explains that the two versions differ over the back of the hand and foot, and then adds more conditions that override שבת: any injury needing evaluation, and a burning fever. רבי אמי says 'internal' starts from the lips inward. That leads to רבי אליעזר's question about gums and teeth. Two proofs are tried and both are pushed aside: אביי's proof from a משנה, and the story of רבי יוחנן, whose צפדינא was treated by a noblewoman. Along the way, the גמרא explains the signs, causes and cures of צפדינא. It then asks how רבי יוחנן could be treated by a non-Jew at all. It concludes that an expert healer would not risk her reputation, while a מין like the one who poisoned רבי אבהו is willing to harm himself. The amud ends with a list of dangerous ailments and their remedies, and begins a story about רבי יעקב that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Second version: no treatment by them for an internal injury
steps.stepSummary: The end of the second version of רבי יוחנן's rule: for a מכה של חלל, one may not be treated by an idolater.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an internal injury, one may not be treated by them.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a rule that started on the previous page. This is the second version (איכא דאמרי) of רבי יוחנן's statement: for an internal injury, you may not get treatment from an idolater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version said: any injury for which we may desecrate שבת may not be treated by them. This second version uses a different measure, a מכה של חלל, meaning an injury inside the body. The גמרא will now ask whether these two versions ever give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: An internal injury, inside the body cavity, treated as possibly life-threatening
One may not be treated (healed) by them, meaning idolaters

phrases.english: An internal injury:
one may not be treated by them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מכה של חלל אין מתרפאין מהן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second version of רבי יוחנן's rule from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a מכה של חלל, one may not be treated by an idolater.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the two versions of רבי יוחנן's rule ever lead to different outcomes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: is there any practical case where the two versions disagree?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One version says 'any injury that overrides שבת' and the other says 'an internal injury'. Most of the time these are the same injuries, so the גמרא wants a case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: He means the two versions of רבי יוחנן's statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the version just finished with the earlier version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the two versions of רבי יוחנן give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: the back of the hand and the back of the foot
steps.stepSummary: The versions differ about the back of the hand and foot, which רב says are like a מכה של חלל for desecrating שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them regarding the back of the hand and the back of the foot. As רב אדא בר מתנה said in the name of רב: the back of the hand and the back of the foot are like an internal injury, and we desecrate שבת for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the two versions split over injuries to the back of the hand or foot. It brings רב's ruling that these injuries are treated like internal ones, so we may desecrate שבת for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first version, any injury that overrides שבת is forbidden to treat through them, and the back of the hand overrides שבת, so it is forbidden. Under the second version, the rule is only for a true internal injury. The back of the hand is only 'like' one, not actually inside the body, so being treated by them would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: We desecrate שבת for them, meaning we may break שבת to treat them
They are like, treated as equal to

steps.confusionAlert: רב does not say the back of the hand IS an internal injury. He says it is LIKE one for שבת. That small word 'like' is exactly why the two versions of רבי יוחנן come out differently.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ גַּב הַיָּד וְגַב הָרֶגֶל,
phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding the back of the hand and the back of the foot,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Adda bar Mattana said that Rav said:
The back of the hand and the back of the foot
are like an internal injury,
and one desecrates Shabbat for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא בינייהו גב היד וגב הרגל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Back of the hand and foot: they override שבת (so the first version forbids being treated by them), but they are not truly internal (so the second version would allow it).

steps.title: Any injury that needs evaluation overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that any injury needing evaluation overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: any injury that needs evaluation, we desecrate שבת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ruling from רב that widens the list of injuries for which we may break שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an injury needs to be checked to know whether it is dangerous, we do not wait. That doubt alone is enough to allow desecrating שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: An evaluation or assessment of how serious the injury is

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a broad practical standard: a possible danger, not only a certain one, allows desecrating שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviyya said that Rav said:
Any injury that requires evaluation,
one desecrates Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב זוטרא בר טוביה אמר רב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling of רב about which injuries override שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any injury that needs evaluation overrides שבת.

steps.title: A burning fever is like an internal injury
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a burning fever counts like a מכה של חלל, so it overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a burning fever is like an internal injury, and we desecrate שבת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: Another case is added to the category: a high, burning fever is treated like an internal injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fever is not a wound at all, yet it is put in the same group as an internal injury because it can be just as dangerous. So the category is defined by danger, not by what the problem looks like.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And this burning fever
is like an internal injury,
and one desecrates Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב שמן בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another condition to the list of things that override שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A burning fever is treated like a מכה של חלל and overrides שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The list of conditions that override שבת grows. The back of the hand and foot and a burning fever are called 'like' a מכה של חלל, and רב adds that any injury needing evaluation also overrides שבת.

steps.title: Where does internal begin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks from what point on the body an injury counts as internal.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is an injury considered an internal injury?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a definition question to set up the next step: where is the boundary between outside and inside the body?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since so much depends on the label מכה של חלל, we need a clear starting line for 'internal'.

phrases.english: From where is it an internal injury?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from listing cases to defining the basic boundary of the category.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical point at which an injury becomes internal.

steps.title: From the lips inward
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains that an internal injury is anything from the lips inward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי explained: from the lips inward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives the boundary: an injury inside the mouth, from the lips inward, counts as internal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This means the inside of the mouth already counts as internal, not only the deep inner organs.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami explained:
From the lip inward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the lips inward is internal.

steps.title: Are gums and teeth internal or external?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks whether problems in the gums and teeth count as internal or external injuries.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר asked: gums and teeth, what is the law? Since they are hard, are they like external injuries? Or perhaps, since they are inside the mouth, are they like internal injuries?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on 'from the lips inward', רבי אליעזר raises a hard case: gums and teeth sit inside the mouth, but they are firm and solid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to look at it. Their hardness makes them seem like outer body parts, which are less dangerous. Their location inside the mouth makes them seem internal.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raised a question that has no easy answer

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer raised a question:
Gums and teeth, what is the law?
Since they are hard,
are they like an external injury,
or perhaps, since they are situated inside,
are they like an internal injury?

steps.triggerLanguage: בעי רבי אליעזר ככי ושיני מאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי אמי's boundary on a borderline case inside the mouth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether gums and teeth follow their hardness (external) or their location (internal).

steps.title: אביי's proof from the toothache and vinegar משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a משנה: one with a toothache may not sip vinegar on שבת. He reads it to mean that with great pain it is allowed, suggesting teeth can count as internal.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: come and hear: one who is bothered by his teeth may not sip vinegar through them. Only someone merely bothered may not, but if it hurts him a lot, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries to answer רבי אליעזר's question from a משנה about healing teeth on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word 'חושש', which sounds like only mild discomfort. אביי reads it carefully: mild discomfort is forbidden, so strong pain must be allowed. That suggests serious tooth pain is treated like an internal injury.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is bothered, has mild pain or concern

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:
One who is bothered by his teeth
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שבת 111a.

phrases.english: may not sip vinegar through them.
It is only one who is bothered who may not,

phrases.aramaic: הָא כָּאֵיב לֵיהּ טוּבָא — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: but if it hurts him a lot, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי תא שמע החושש בשיניו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve רבי אליעזר's question.
steps.raayaObject: That teeth with serious pain are treated like a מכה של חלל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת about sipping vinegar for a toothache, read through the word 'חושש'.

steps.title: Rejected: 'bothered' may include great pain
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside: maybe the תנא uses 'חושש' even for strong pain, so nothing is learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the תנא calls even a case where it hurts him a lot 'bothered'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects אביי's proof by questioning how he read the word 'חושש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's proof depended on 'חושש' meaning only mild pain. If the תנא uses that word for any pain, even severe, then the משנה forbids all cases and proves nothing about teeth being internal. רבי אליעזר's question is still unanswered, so the next step tries a new proof.
steps.whatToRemember: The question of gums and teeth is not settled by אביי's proof, because the word 'חושש' might cover even strong pain.

phrases.english: Perhaps the tanna
where it hurts him a lot
also calls it 'bothered'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דלמא תנא היכא דכאיב ליה טובא חושש נמי קרי ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'חושש' means only mild pain, but the תנא may use it for severe pain too.

steps.title: The story of רבי יוחנן and the noblewoman's cure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells how רבי יוחנן, sick with צפדינא, was treated by a noblewoman. She taught him the cure so he could use it on שבת if he needed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן suffered from צפדינא. He went to a certain noblewoman, and she treated him on Thursday and Friday. He asked her: What about tomorrow (שבת)? She said: You will not need it. He asked: And if I do need it, what then? She said: Swear to me that you will not reveal it. He swore: 'To the God of Israel I will not reveal it.' She revealed it to him, and the next day he went out and taught it in his public lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof, in the form of a story, for the question of whether gum disease counts as an internal injury. This step only tells the story. The actual conclusion comes a few steps later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צפדינא is a disease of the gums and teeth, which is exactly the case רבי אליעזר asked about. רבי יוחנן wanted to know how to treat it on שבת, and she gave him the recipe so he could prepare it himself. That suggests treating it on שבת is allowed, the way it is for an internal injury.

keyTerms.meaning: A disease of the gums and teeth (often understood as scurvy)
A noblewoman, here a non-Jewish healer
He taught it in his public lecture

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at the end of the story looking for the proof. The גמרא first deals with the oath problem, and it only states what we learn from the story in step 16 (אלמא).

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yochanan suffered from tzafdina,
he went to a certain noblewoman,
she treated him on Thursday and Friday.
He said to her: What about tomorrow?
She said to him: You will not need it.
If I do need it, what then?
She said: Swear to me that you will not reveal it.
He swore to her:
"To the God of Israel, I will not reveal it."
She revealed it to him,
the next day he went out and taught it in his public lecture.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חָשׁ בְּצַפְדִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's proof from the משנה was pushed aside, the גמרא tries a new proof from a story.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a gum or tooth disease counts as an internal injury that may be treated on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יוחנן, who learned the cure for צפדינא so he could make it himself on שבת.

steps.title: How could he reveal the secret after swearing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's behavior: he swore not to reveal the cure, yet he taught it publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he swore to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the main proof to ask a side question. How could רבי יוחנן go back on his oath?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching the cure in public seems to break the oath he had just made. A great חכם like רבי יוחנן would never break a שבועה, so the story needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But he swore to her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a detail in the story of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן publicly teaching the cure after swearing not to reveal it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An oath not to reveal something is broken by teaching it in public.

steps.title: His oath was worded carefully
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that his oath only promised not to reveal it 'to the God of Israel', which still left him free to tell the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said, 'To the God of Israel I will not reveal it,' meaning: but to His people Israel I will reveal it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the exact words of the oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She heard it as a normal oath 'by the God of Israel'. His words actually meant 'I will not reveal it to God', which makes no sense as a promise, since God already knows. So he never promised to keep it from people.

phrases.english: "To the God of Israel I will not reveal it",
but to His people Israel I will reveal it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Careful reading of the oath's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He swore never to reveal the cure to anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only swore not to reveal it 'to God', so telling the Jewish people did not break the oath.

steps.title: Isn't this still a חילול השם?
steps.stepSummary: Even if he technically kept his oath, the noblewoman will think a great Jewish חכם broke his word. Isn't that a חילול השם?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a desecration of God's name!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Even if the oath was not broken, it still looks bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She does not know about the clever wording. From her point of view, a famous rabbi swore and then broke his oath, and that would make ה׳'s name look bad.

keyTerms.meaning: Desecration of God's name, making ה׳ or His people look bad

phrases.english: But there is a desecration of God's name!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13: the wording may save the oath, but not the public impression.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that his oath was cleverly worded.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The noblewoman would still believe he broke his oath, which causes a חילול השם.

steps.title: He told her from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן made it clear to her right away that his oath did not stop him from sharing the cure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He revealed this to her at the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the side discussion. There was no חילול השם because he was honest with her from the beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she knew what his words really meant, she could not feel tricked or think he broke his word. That ends the side questions, and the גמרא can return to the main proof.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, at the outset

phrases.english: That he revealed it to her at the outset.
phrases.notes: He means he told her right away that his oath would not stop him from sharing the cure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 and ends the side discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She thought he broke his oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: He told her right away what his oath meant, so there was no חילול השם.

steps.title: So gum disease is like an internal injury
steps.stepSummary: Back to the main question: the story shows that a gum disease is treated like an internal injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: Apparently, it is like an internal injury.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its proof and states what it learns from the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was prepared to make the cure himself on שבת, so treating צפדינא must be allowed on שבת. That only makes sense if a disease in the gums counts as an internal injury.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently, so we see (introduces a conclusion drawn from a source)
An internal injury, inside the body

phrases.english: Apparently, it is like an internal injury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the oath discussion to complete the proof begun in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: Gum and tooth disease counts as an internal injury.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's plan to prepare the cure for צפדינא on שבת.

steps.title: צפדינא is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof: צפדינא is different because it starts in the mouth but ends in the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: צפדינא is different, since it begins in the mouth and ends in the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from the story is pushed aside. It does not answer the general question about gums and teeth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צפדינא spreads to the intestines, so it is treated as an internal illness even while it is still in the mouth. An ordinary gum or tooth problem does not spread like that, so רבי אליעזר's question stays unanswered.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs (אביי's משנה and the story of רבי יוחנן) were pushed aside. Whether ordinary gum and tooth problems count as internal remains an open question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a disease which spreads inward is treated as internal from its very start, even while it is still in the mouth.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Tzafdina is different,
since it begins in the mouth
and ends in the intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: שָׁאנֵי צַפְדִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion drawn in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from צפדינא for all gum and tooth problems, but agrees that צפדינא itself is treated as internal.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: צפדינא is a unique disease that spreads to the intestines, so it cannot teach us about ordinary gum and tooth problems.

steps.title: The symptoms of צפדינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to recognize צפדינא and answers that the gums bleed when something is placed between the teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is its sign? When one puts something between the teeth, blood comes from the rows of teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: The main argument is over. The גמרא now adds side information about the disease, starting with how to recognize it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is practical background, not part of the argument. Bleeding from the gums when something touches the teeth is the sign of צפדינא.

phrases.english: What is its sign?
One places something between the teeth,
and blood comes from the rows of teeth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the halachic discussion ends, the גמרא adds background about the disease.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bleeding from the gums when something is placed between the teeth.

steps.title: What causes צפדינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists three causes: very cold wheat foods, very hot barley foods, and leftover fried fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what does it come? From very cold wheat foods, from very hot barley foods, and from the leftovers of fried fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the side information and explains what causes the disease.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three kinds of food are blamed: wheat food eaten very cold, barley food eaten very hot, and leftover fried fish. This is health advice, not הלכה.

phrases.english: From what does it come?
From very cold wheat foods,
and from very hot barley foods,
and from the leftovers of a dish of fried fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the background about צפדינא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Very cold wheat foods, very hot barley foods, and leftover fried fish.

steps.title: The cure the noblewoman used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the noblewoman did for רבי יוחנן. רבי אחא בריה דרבא says leaven water, olive oil, and salt. מר בר רב אשי says goose fat applied with a goose feather.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did she do for him? רבי אחא the son of רבא said: Leaven water, olive oil, and salt. מר בר רב אשי said: Goose fat, applied with a goose feather.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the side discussion by telling us the actual cure from the story, with two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finally reveals the 'secret' that רבי יוחנן taught in public. The two אמוראים disagree about what the remedy was.

keyTerms.meaning: Water in which leaven (sourdough) was soaked

phrases.english: What did she do for him?
phrases.notes: 'She' is the noblewoman from the story in step 11.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha the son of Rava said:
Leaven water, olive oil, and salt,
and Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
Goose fat, with a goose's wing feather.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the background about צפדינא by naming the cure from the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What remedy the noblewoman used on רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two opinions: leaven water, olive oil, and salt; or goose fat applied with a goose feather.

steps.title: אביי's cure that finally worked
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the earlier cures did not help him. An Arab taught him to burn unripe olive pits on a new hoe and press them onto the gums, and that cured him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I tried all of these cures and was not healed, until a certain Arab told me: Bring olive pits that are less than a third ripe, burn them on a new hoe, and stick them along the row of gums. I did this and was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds one more cure for צפדינא from his own experience. This wraps up the medical list before the גמרא turns to a halachic question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 listed the noblewoman's remedies. אביי says none of those worked for him and gives a different cure that did. It is practical information, not an argument.

phrases.english: Abaye said: I did all of them
and was not healed,
until a certain Arab told me:
Bring pits of olives
that have not filled out a third,
phrases.notes: Literally "not filled a third": olives less than one-third ripe.

phrases.english: and burn them on a new hoe,
and stick them along the row of the gums.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket word and some don't; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: I did so and was healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי: אנא עבדי כולהו ולא איתסאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final, successful remedy after the noblewoman's cures in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unripe olive pits burned on a new hoe and pressed onto the gums cure צפדינא.

steps.title: How could רבי יוחנן be treated by a non-Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן let a non-Jewish noblewoman treat him, since he himself ruled that an illness serious enough to override שבת may not be treated by non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how could רבי יוחנן do this? Didn't רבה בר בר חנה say in the name of רבי יוחנן: For any wound that we desecrate שבת to treat, one may not be healed by non-Jews!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the story: it seems to go against רבי יוחנן's own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that צפדינא is treated like an internal injury, which overrides שבת. רבי יוחנן ruled that for such dangerous illnesses we may not use a non-Jewish healer, because he might harm the patient. Yet רבי יוחנן himself went to a non-Jewish noblewoman.

keyTerms.meaning: We break שבת (to save a life)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the challenge is to רבי יוחנן's actions, not to his ruling. The ruling stays; the גמרא only asks why his own case was allowed.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan, how could he do this?
phrases.notes: This refers to the story of the noblewoman treating רבי יוחנן's צפדינא.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar bar Ḥana say
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מַכָּה שֶׁמְּחַלְּלִין עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: Any wound for which we desecrate Shabbat
one may not be healed by them!

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי יוחנן היכי עביד הכי? והאמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story of רבי יוחנן and the noblewoman and questions it on halachic grounds.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's choice to be treated by a non-Jewish noblewoman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: צפדינא overrides שבת, and רבי יוחנן ruled that such illnesses may not be treated by non-Jews, so his behavior contradicts his own ruling.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן was an important person, and a non-Jew would not dare to harm him.
steps.simpleTranslation: An important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a quick answer: the ban does not apply to an important person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban exists because a non-Jewish healer might secretly harm a Jewish patient. With a famous, important person, the healer would be afraid of the consequences, so the danger is gone.

phrases.english: An important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule: an exception for an important person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on non-Jewish healers applies to everyone, including רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: An important person may be treated, since the healer would not dare to harm him.

steps.title: But רבי אבהו was important and was still attacked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: רבי אבהו was important, yet יעקב the מין put poison on his leg, and his leg was saved only because רבי אמי and רבי אסי licked it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אבהו was an important person, and יעקב the מין put a drug on his leg. If not for רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who licked his leg, he would have had to have his leg cut off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to disprove the idea that important people are safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 23 said nobody would dare harm an important person. Here an important person was harmed on purpose, so being important does not seem to protect anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: A drug or salve (here, a poison)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, דְּאָדָם חָשׁוּב הֲוָה,
phrases.english: But Rabbi Abbahu, who was an important person,
and Ya'akov the heretic placed for him
a drug on his leg,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: and if not for Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
who licked his leg,
his leg would have been cut off!

steps.triggerLanguage: והא רבי אבהו דאדם חשוב הוה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 23 with a counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an important person is safe from a non-Jewish healer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אבהו was important and was still poisoned, so importance does not protect.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's healer was an expert doctor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reason: the noblewoman who treated רבי יוחנן was an expert doctor, and she would not ruin her reputation by harming a patient.
steps.simpleTranslation: The healer of רבי יוחנן was an expert doctor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new answer for רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of looking at the patient, the גמרא now looks at the healer. A known expert has a name to protect, so she would not risk harming a patient.

phrases.english: The one of Rabbi Yoḥanan was an expert doctor,
phrases.notes: "The one of רבי יוחנן" is the noblewoman who treated him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 24 weakened the answer of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the healer's status
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was allowed only because he was important.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was allowed because his healer was an expert who would not risk her name.

steps.title: But רבי אבהו's healer was also an expert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the one who treated רבי אבהו was also an expert doctor, and still harmed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The healer of רבי אבהו was also an expert doctor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the new answer still does not separate the two stories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being an expert keeps a healer from causing harm, יעקב the מין should not have poisoned רבי אבהו. So the gap between the cases is still not explained.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ נָמֵי רוֹפֵא מוּמְחֶה הֲוָה,
phrases.english: The one of Rabbi Abbahu was also an expert doctor,

steps.triggerLanguage: דרבי אבהו נמי רופא מומחה הוה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an expert healer would not harm a patient
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יעקב the מין was also an expert, yet he poisoned רבי אבהו.

steps.title: מינים are willing to harm themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's final answer: רבי אבהו's case is different, because מינים think 'Let me die with the Philistines'. They will ruin themselves just to hurt Jews, but an ordinary non-Jewish expert will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו is different, because the מינים take on themselves the attitude of 'Let me die with the Philistines.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the back-and-forth by showing what made רבי אבהו's attacker unusual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The expert-healer answer still holds. It failed with רבי אבהו only because his attacker was a מין, driven by religious hatred and ready to lose everything, like שמשון. An ordinary non-Jewish expert, like רבי יוחנן's noblewoman, would protect her reputation, so his treatment was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They take it on themselves / that is their attitude
"Let me die with the Philistines", שמשון's words

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן ruled that a dangerous illness may not be treated by a non-Jew. He himself was treated by an expert non-Jewish healer, who would not risk her name. רבי אבהו's case is different because a מין will harm himself just to hurt a Jew.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows when a non-Jewish expert healer may be trusted. It depends on whether the healer has a reason to protect himself, and a מין does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu is different
because heretics take on themselves regarding him
"Let me die with the Philistines."

steps.triggerLanguage: שאני רבי אבהו דמוקמי ביה מיני בנפשייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 and saves the expert-healer answer of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the attacker's motive
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An expert healer never harms a patient, so רבי אבהו's case breaks the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: An expert protects his name, but a מין will sacrifice himself to hurt Jews, so רבי אבהו's case is an exception.

steps.title: A sword gash is dangerous enough to break שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a gash from a sword counts as a danger to life, so one may break שבת to treat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: This kind of gash is dangerous, and we may break שבת to treat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from שמואל: a sword gash is a life-threatening wound. Because of that, treating it on שבת is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the larger discussion of which wounds count as a סכנה. Once a wound is a real danger, the normal rules of שבת are pushed aside to treat it. It also sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks what the treatment actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: A gash or deep cut, such as from a sword
We may break the laws of שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical example of the rule that danger to life overrides שבת.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
This gash is a danger,
and we may desecrate Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַאי פְּדַעְתָּא סַכַּנְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the story-based debate about being treated by non-Jews and begins a list of ailments and their remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sword gash is a danger to life, so one may break שבת to treat it.

steps.title: The remedy for a gash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the remedy is and answers: cress in vinegar stops the bleeding, and certain scrapings or trash worms help the flesh grow back.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the remedy? To stop the bleeding, cress soaked in vinegar. To make the flesh grow back, scrapings of יבלא and of a thornbush, or worms from the trash heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how to treat the gash and gives a two-part remedy. One part stops the blood, and the other helps new flesh grow over the wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The remedy is split by goal. First stop the bleeding, then heal the wound. There is a different ingredient for each stage, and a second choice for the healing stage.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring up, here meaning to make new flesh grow

phrases.english: What is its remedy?
To stop the blood: cress in vinegar,
to bring up new flesh:
scrapings of yavla and scrapings of thornbush,
phrases.notes: יבלא is some kind of plant, and we can't be sure exactly which.

phrases.english: or worms from the trash heap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and gives the treatment for the wound שמואל just called dangerous.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the treatment for a sword gash?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cress in vinegar stops the bleeding. Scrapings of יבלא and thornbush, or trash worms, help the flesh grow back.

steps.title: Grape-like boils come before death
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא teaches that grape-like boils are a forerunner of מלאך המות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: These grape-like boils are the forerunner of מלאך המות.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא names another serious ailment, a boil shaped like a grape. He warns that it often comes right before death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it a forerunner of מלאך המות shows how dangerous this ailment is. It is not a minor skin problem. This sets up the remedy in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A grape, here a boil shaped like a grape
Forerunner, one who goes ahead to announce someone

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
This grape-like boil
is the forerunner of the Angel of Death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ailment to the list after שמואל's gash.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grape-like boils are a deadly warning sign.

steps.title: The remedy for grape-like boils
steps.stepSummary: The remedy is טיגנא in honey or parsley in wine. While these soak, one rubs a grape of the same size and color on the boil.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the remedy? A טיגנא plant in honey, or parsley in wine. Meanwhile, bring a grape the same size and roll it on the boil: a white grape for a white boil and a black grape for a black boil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the main cure for the boil. It also gives something to do while waiting for the cure to be ready.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main remedy is a plant soaked in honey or wine, which takes time. So the גמרא adds a stopgap: rub a matching grape on the boil, matching both its size and its color.

keyTerms.meaning: Of its kind, here meaning of the same size

phrases.english: What is its remedy?
tigna in honey,
or parsley in wine.
In the meantime,
let him bring a grape of its kind (the same size)
and roll it over it,
phrases.notes: Some versions spell it the way it is in round brackets; the square-bracket spelling is the corrected one. Both mean 'on it.'

phrases.english: a white one for a white one
and a black one for a black one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the treatment for the boil רב ספרא just described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the cure for grape-like boils?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טיגנא in honey or parsley in wine. Meanwhile, rub on a grape of matching size and color.

steps.title: An abscess comes before fever
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a certain abscess is a forerunner of fever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This abscess is the forerunner of fever.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא adds another ailment, an abscess. He says it often leads to a fever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא uses the same 'forerunner' wording as רב ספרא, but here the abscess warns of fever, not death. This sets up the remedy that comes next.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This abscess is the forerunner of fever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי סִימְטָא פַּרְוַונְקָא דְּאִשָּׁתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third ailment to the list, using the same 'forerunner' wording as רב ספרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An abscess is a warning sign of fever.

steps.title: The remedy for an abscess
steps.stepSummary: One should flick the abscess sixty times and then cut it open lengthwise and crosswise.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the remedy? Flick it sixty times with the fingers, and then tear it open lengthwise and crosswise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the treatment for רבא's abscess. First flick it many times, then cut it open in a cross shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treatment has two stages, flicking it and then opening it. Opening it lengthwise and crosswise means making a cross-shaped cut.

keyTerms.meaning: Flicks or snaps of the fingers
Lengthwise and crosswise (like threads in a weave)

phrases.english: What is its remedy?
He should strike it with sixty finger-flicks,
and tear it lengthwise and crosswise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the treatment for the abscess רבא just described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do we treat this abscess?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Flick it sixty times, then cut it open lengthwise and crosswise.

steps.title: When an abscess is not a concern
steps.stepSummary: The danger and treatment apply only when the head of the abscess has not turned white. Once it is white, there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only when its head has not turned white. But if its head has turned white, we have no concern with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the previous teaching. Only an abscess whose head has not whitened is a warning sign that needs treatment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A white head is a sign the abscess is already healing. So the warning about fever, and the need to cut it open, do not apply then.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no concern with it

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא names an ailment and gives its remedy. רבא's abscess is a concern only before its head turns white.

phrases.english: And these words apply when its head has not whitened,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חִיוָּר רֵישֵׁיהּ לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if its head has whitened, we have no concern with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's warning and treatment to an abscess that has not yet whitened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an abscess with a non-white head is dangerous. A white-headed one is healing and is no concern.

steps.title: A new story about רבי יעקב begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: רבי יעקב was suffering from an ailment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב suffered (from an ailment)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: a story about רבי יעקב being sick. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only the opening words of a new story. The details of his illness and what was done for it come next, so nothing has been concluded yet.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov suffered

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that continues the medical theme of the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup line only: רבי יעקב was ill, and the details follow.
